papers.title: Biodegradable WE43 Magnesium Alloy Produced by Selective Laser Melting: Mechanical Properties, Corrosion Behavior, and In-Vitro Cytotoxicity
papers.abstract: In this work, selective laser melting (SLM) technology was used to prepare Mg-4Y-3Nd-Zr (WE43) alloy. This alloy and production method are promising for the design of biodegradable implants. The aim of this study was to investigate the chemical composition, microstructure, mechanical properties, corrosion behavior in simulated body fluid (SBF), and cytotoxicity of the alloy produced by SLM method and to compare it with conventionally gravity cast reference alloy. Analysis of the surface of the revealed an oxygen content of 7 wt.%. Undesirable unmelted and only partially adhered spherical particles of the starting powder were also found. The microstructure of the material was very fine and consisted of α-Mg dendritic matrix, β-Mg41(Nd, Y)5 intermetallic phase, Y2O3 inclusions, and 0.6 vol.% of residual porosity. The Vickers hardness, compressive yield strength, compressive strength, and maximum compressive strain were 88 HV0.1, 201 MPa, 394 MPa, and 14%, respectively, which are close to the reference values in as-cast. The in vitro corrosion rates determined by immersion and potentiodynamic tests were 2.6 mm/year and 1.3 mm/year, respectively. Cytotoxicity tests indicated good biocompatibility of the 3D-printed alloy.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究SLM制备的WE43镁合金的力学性能和腐蚀行为，但未涉及多孔结构设计或应力屏蔽分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not analyze porous structure design, stress shielding, fatigue, or osseointegration, which are central to the AM Biomedical Materials direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 表征SLM制备WE43镁合金的力学、腐蚀和生物相容性。
summary_zh.method: 采用SLM工艺制备WE43合金，测试其微观结构、力学性能、腐蚀速率和细胞毒性。
summary_zh.result: SLM制备的WE43合金力学性能接近铸态，腐蚀速率适中，生物相容性良好。
summary_zh.validation: 通过压缩测试、浸泡腐蚀、动电位极化及细胞毒性实验进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To characterize the mechanical properties, corrosion behavior, and biocompatibility of SLM-fabricated WE43 magnesium alloy for biodegradable implant applications.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting was used to produce WE43 alloy, followed by microstructure analysis, mechanical testing, corrosion tests in SBF, and cytotoxicity assays.
summary_en.result: The SLM-processed WE43 exhibited mechanical properties comparable to cast material, with a compressive strength of 394 MPa, corrosion rate of 2.6 mm/year, and good biocompatibility.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed via Vickers hardness, compressive tests, immersion and potentiodynamic corrosion tests, and in vitro cytotoxicity testing.

papers.title: The effect of laser power and scanning speed on forming structure in selective laser melting process
papers.abstract: Abstract With the continuous development of ship technology, the usage environment of some parts has changed, with higher requirements for materials and preparation technology being put forward. Some traditional structural materials have do not meet the actual working conditions of ships, which necessitates development of new materials and research on their preparation technology. Owing to its high strength and stable mechanical properties at high temperature, molybdenum base alloy is expected to replace nickel base alloy and aluminum base alloy the primary structural material in the development of ships. Under the conventional method, the impurity elements is quite complex and there are limitations in the shape of the formed parts. This experiment uses spherical pure molybdenum powder as raw material. The effects of laser power, powder thickness, scanning speed and scanning distance on the microstructure of formed parts during selective laser melting process were studied and the optimum process parameters were determined. Laser power and scanning speed can seriously affect the quality of the forming parts. In this experiment, by comparing the density and internal holes of the forming parts under different process parameters, the best preparation process for the forming parts was determined: laser power 325 watts, scanning speed 400 mm s −1 , powder thickness 30 μ m, scanning distance 40 μ m. Meanwhile, the forming workpiece density is the largest, up to 94.92%.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究钼基合金的选区激光熔化工艺参数对成形质量的影响，应用于船舶制造，与生物医学植入物的力学适配性、疲劳性能及骨整合无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on SLM process parameters for molybdenum alloy in shipbuilding, with no biomedical implant application, no porous structure design for stress shielding, no fatigue testing, and no surface roughness or osseointegration analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索钼基合金选区激光熔化工艺参数对成形质量的影响
summary_zh.method: 采用球形纯钼粉末，改变激光功率、扫描速度等参数进行成形实验
summary_zh.result: 优化工艺参数后成形件密度最高达94.92%
summary_zh.validation: 通过密度测量和内部孔隙观察验证工艺参数

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effects of laser power and scanning speed on the forming quality of molybdenum alloy parts fabricated by selective laser melting for ship applications.
summary_en.method: Spherical pure molybdenum powder was used, and experiments were conducted with varying laser power, scanning speed, powder thickness, and scanning distance.
summary_en.result: Optimal process parameters (laser power 325 W, scanning speed 400 mm/s) yielded a maximum density of 94.92%.
summary_en.validation: Density measurement and internal hole observation were used to validate the forming quality under different process conditions.

papers.title: Open-source syringe extrusion head for shear-thinning materials 3D printing
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to report the development of an open-source syringe extrusion head for shear-thinning materials. The target is to adapt open-source 3D printers to be helpful in research lines that use gels, hydrogels, pastes, inks, and bio-inks. Design/methodology/approach This hardware was designed to be compatible with a Graber i3-based 3D printer; nevertheless, it can be easily adapted to other open-source 3D printers. Findings The extrusion head successfully deposits the material during the 3D printing process. It was validated fabricating geometries that include scaffold structures, which are a possible application of bioprinting for tissue engineering. As reported, the extruded filaments allowed the porous samples' structuration. Practical implications This system expands the applications of open-source 3D printers used at the laboratory scale. It enables low-cost access to research areas such as tissue engineering and biofabrication, energy storage devices and food 3D printing. Originality/value The open-source hardware here reported is of simple fabrication, assembly and installation. It uses a Cardan coupling and a three guides system to transfer the stepper motor motion. This approach allows continuous movement transfer to the syringe piston, producing an adequate deposition or retraction. Thus, the effect of misalignments is avoided, considering that these latter can cause skipping steps in the motor, directly affecting the deposition.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文仅涉及硬件设计，未涉及任何AI或数据驱动方法，与AI生物打印方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper describes only a mechanical syringe extrusion head for 3D printing; it contains no AI/ML integration, no bioprinting workflow stage optimization, and no experimental validation of AI-based control.

summary_zh.motivation: 为剪切变稀材料开发开源注射挤出机头，降低生物打印硬件门槛。
summary_zh.method: 设计兼容Graber i3打印机的挤压头，采用万向联轴器和三导轨系统传递运动。
summary_zh.result: 成功沉积材料并制造多孔支架结构，验证了挤出系统的可行性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过打印支架结构进行实物验证，评估挤丝和孔隙形成。

summary_en.motivation: To develop an open-source syringe extrusion head for shear-thinning materials, enabling low-cost bioprinting research.
summary_en.method: The extrusion head uses a Cardan coupling and three-guide system to transfer stepper motor motion continuously to the syringe piston, designed for Graber i3-based printers.
summary_en.result: The system successfully deposited materials and fabricated scaffold structures with controlled porosity, demonstrating functional extrusion.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed by printing porous scaffold geometries and assessing filament deposition and structuration.

papers.title: Risk of early implant failure in grafted and non-grafted sites: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess whether bone grafting is associated with early implant failure (defined as a lack of osseointegration detected prior to functional loading) and to evaluate the association between bone grafting procedures and other risk factors for early implant failure. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two independent reviewers conducted an electronic search of MEDLINE (via PubMed). Meta-analysis was performed for the odds ratio of bone grafting procedures associated with early implant failure. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies was used to assess the risk of bias. RESULTS: Of the 231 articles selected for full-text review, 10 were included in the qualitative analysis and for quantitative meta-analysis. An odds ratio of 1.50 (95% confidence interval 1.06-2.13) was recorded for bone grafting procedures associated with early implant failure. Data regarding the association of bone grafting and other risk factors in determining early implant failure were insufficient for quantitative analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Within the limitations of this study, a significant positive association was found between bone grafting procedures and early implant failure. The possible negative effect of bone grafting procedures on implant osseointegration should be considered when planning implant therapy.
papers.venue: International journal of oral implantology (Berlin, Germany)

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为临床系统综述，未涉及增材制造或生物力学评价，与用户研究方向无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: No AM fabrication, no mechanical testing, no stress shielding analysis, and no bone-implant interface quantification.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估骨移植是否与早期种植体失败相关。
summary_zh.method: 对10项研究进行定量荟萃分析，计算骨移植的优势比。
summary_zh.result: 骨移植与早期种植体失败显著正相关（OR=1.50）。
summary_zh.validation: 采用纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表评估偏倚风险。

summary_en.motivation: To determine whether bone grafting procedures are associated with a higher risk of early implant failure.
summary_en.method: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 cohort studies with meta-analysis of odds ratios.
summary_en.result: Bone grafting showed a statistically significant increased odds of early implant failure (OR=1.50, 95% CI 1.06-2.13).
summary_en.validation: Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and results were based on clinical data from included studies.
